instructions: Elcano Lens classifies websites, iOS apps, Android apps and CTV apps into advertising quality tiers (Premium / Standard / Long Tail / Failed) with IAB categories, language, political leaning, audience size and optional custom questions. Workflow: create_job -> get_job until status is completed -> get_job_results for a summary and rows -> get_download_link(file='output') for the full CSV. Jobs run in the background and take from a minute (a few domains) to hours (tens of thousands); never create a second job for the same list while one is queued or running. For a short list pass items; for a CSV/XLSX in the workspace pass content_base64 as a workspace file reference with filename; for a file already uploaded to Lens pass input_file (see list_input_files). Jobs spend real OpenRouter money, so confirm large runs with the user first. The defaults are recommended: only set models or turn off deep_retry / research_fallback when the user asks.

tools.name: create_job
tools.title: Start a Lens classification job
tools.description: Queue a Lens job that classifies websites, iOS/Android apps or CTV apps. Give exactly one input: items (identifiers such as 'nytimes.com', '284882215' or 'com.spotify.music'), content_base64 + filename (a .csv/.xlsx; prefer a workspace file reference), or input_file (a file already in the Lens library). Returns the job with its id; poll get_job until it completes. The run spends OpenRouter credit.

name.description: Run name shown in the Lens dashboard, e.g. 'Q4 allowlist review'.

items.description: Domains, App Store ids or Android package names, one per entry.

content_base64.description: The input file's bytes (CSV or XLSX), base64-encoded. Requires filename. Lens finds the identifier column itself (Domain, url, pageURL, app_id, Bundle ID for CTV).

filename.description: Name for the uploaded file, ending .csv or .xlsx.

input_file.description: Name of a file already in the Lens input library (list_input_files).

ctv.description: Force the CTV workflow. Lens detects CTV lists by their columns, so this is rarely needed.

custom_categories.description: Optional extra questions answered per row, as {"categories": [{"name", "type": "boolean"|"choice", "question", "options"?}]} (max 12). get_options shows an example.

research_fallback.description: Classify unscrapeable sites from web research (default true).

deep_retry.description: Retry failed sites with headless Chrome (default true; slow on big lists).

tools.name: get_job
tools.title: Check a Lens job
tools.description: Status, progress (processed/total, successes, errors), estimated seconds remaining, spend so far, settings, available files and, for failed jobs, the log tail.

job_id.description: Lens job id, e.g. 20261015143000-a1b2c3 (from create_job or list_jobs).

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.title: List Lens jobs
tools.description: Recent Lens jobs, newest first, from every source (dashboard, CLI, API).

tools.name: get_job_results
tools.title: Read a Lens job's results
tools.description: Summary counts (by quality tier, content type and top IAB tier 1) over the whole output plus a page of rows. Filter with quality (e.g. 'Premium'), pick columns, page with offset/limit. Works on running jobs too (rows written so far). For the full file use get_download_link.

job_id.description: Lens job id, e.g. 20261015143000-a1b2c3 (from create_job or list_jobs).

limit.description: Rows to return (default 25; 0 for the summary only).

quality.description: Only rows with this Quality value: Premium, Standard, Long Tail or Failed.

tools.name: get_download_link
tools.title: Get a download link for a Lens file
tools.description: A short-lived (15 minute), single-file URL for a job's output CSV, run log, input list or custom-category definitions. Fetch it into the workspace with download_url; it needs no credentials.

job_id.description: Lens job id, e.g. 20261015143000-a1b2c3 (from create_job or list_jobs).

annotations.title: Get a download link for a Lens file

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.title: Cancel a Lens job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running job. A running job stops after its current items; rows already written stay in its output.

job_id.description: Lens job id, e.g. 20261015143000-a1b2c3 (from create_job or list_jobs).

tools.name: list_input_files
tools.title: List Lens input files
tools.description: Files in the Lens input library, newest first, with how many websites/apps/CTV rows each holds.

tools.name: get_options
tools.title: Lens job options
tools.description: Default and selectable models, limits, the custom-categories format and the output CSV columns. Call it before overriding a model or writing custom categories.
